scenarios.name: source guard, role and ACL keep the extracted profile step internal
101 profiles sharing one timestamp: 100 independent commits then the remaining profile without skips
30-second cutoff includes its exact boundary once and excludes recent or inactive/non-worker profiles
one profile queues only 200 newest eligible Needs in the same transaction as its cursor
existing world, ownership, expiry, closure, status and already-reconsidered filters match the unchanged owner
LADDER preserves a running wave; ALL requeues it without changing its status, attempts or earlier run time
a mid-profile enqueue error rolls back its earlier writes and cursor; a later retry completes once
invalid time/watermark and missing configuration do not move the cursor or enqueue work
busy watermark is skipped without changing a profile or holding an unrelated queue lock
two native schedulers share the keyset cursor without processing the same timestamp/account twice
backend termination after first profile COMMIT preserves200 queue writes and resumes with a fresh client
an explicit outer transaction rejects the first internal COMMIT and rolls back profile plus queue
time budget yields after the first completed profile and preserves the remaining cursor work

limitations: Synthetic rows in an isolated captured SQL graph, not a full Supabase clone or real user/device traffic.
Actual captured profile requeue predicate, account-world and queue upsert bodies execute on PostgreSQL17; app profile/Need seeding bypasses application writers deliberately.
Probe triggers and an explicitly marked post-COMMIT advisory barrier observe transaction/session ordering; they are never added to the candidate or hosted server.
The process-failure scenario terminates a local PostgreSQL client backend after one commit, then resumes using a fresh connection and durable cursor. It does not stop the whole PostgreSQL server.
This change proves profile-sweep transaction boundaries, not hosted throughput, 300000-user capacity, Expo/FCM or native Android.
The100 profile and200 Need limits are per invocation/profile; concurrent calls do not add a new fleet-global quota.
The30-second cutoff retains the existing assumption that a profile write commits within30 seconds of its updated_at. Unbounded older long-running writers remain outside this contract.
Five other marketplace maintenance phases, their error and partial-progress semantics, hosted role/security and Cron switch acceptance still gate R13 activation. Source guard remains active.
